summary: Self-improving ML experimentation loop: agent edits a training script, runs a time-boxed job, measures improvement, keeps or discards the change, and repeats. Accumulated 66k+ stars after March 2026 release.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — the Karpathy Loop pattern (edit→evaluate→keep/discard) is structurally similar to AgentForge's state machine, but the repo targets ML training pipelines, not software-dev agent orchestration. No verified gap it would close.

summary: Open-ended self-improving agent that iteratively modifies its own source code and validates each mutation empirically on coding benchmarks; accepted at ICLR 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — falls squarely in the 'prompt self-evolution' and RL-training-loop red-flag category from Phase 3 constraints. Requires an archive of agent variants and continuous benchmark evaluation infrastructure not present in AgentForge.

summary: Neuroscience-inspired 7-layer memory architecture for autonomous AI systems including sensory, working, episodic, semantic, procedural, associative, and metacognitive layers.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — thematically relevant to agent memory, but HID-188 already tracks cross-run episodic memory injection. No new gap over what HID-188 covers.

source: Escher-Loop: Mutual Evolution by Closed-Loop Self-Referential Optimization (arxiv 2604.23472)
summary: Closed-loop self-referential optimization where agents and evaluators co-evolve, enabling open-ended self-improvement without fixed benchmarks.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — self-referential evolution and co-evolving evaluators fall into the 'prompt self-evolution' disqualification category. Requires infrastructure AgentForge explicitly defers.

source: State of AI Agent Memory 2026 (mem0.ai report)
summary: Industry survey showing episodic+semantic+working memory as the dominant three-tier pattern for production agent memory in 2026, with cross-session persistence via vector stores.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — validates the importance of episodic memory, but AgentForge already tracks this in HID-188. No new actionable gap.

source: OpenAI Agents SDK sandbox and subagents update (2026)
summary: OpenAI added native sandbox execution, a model-native harness, and subagent support to its Agents SDK; works with 100+ LLMs via Chat Completions API.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses its own CLI subprocess model (ProcessRunner spawning claude/codex CLIs), not the OpenAI SDK. Sandboxing at the CLI level is handled differently. No directly applicable gap.

source: Microsoft Agent Framework (AutoGen + Semantic Kernel consolidation)
summary: Microsoft placed AutoGen and Semantic Kernel into maintenance mode and consolidated both into a new Microsoft Agent Framework integrating with Azure AI Foundry for observability and responsible AI.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — enterprise Azure-first framework; AgentForge uses Fastify + Prisma + Linear/GitHub integrations with CLI subprocess agents. Architecture and target deployment are incompatible.

summary: LangGraph reached version 1.2.6 in August 2026; no major new architectural capability identified beyond incremental improvements to graph execution and streaming.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — LangGraph's graph-based orchestration model differs from AgentForge's deterministic state machine. No new gap identified vs. what's already tracked in the open backlog.

source: Episodic-Semantic Memory for Long-Horizon Scientific Agents (arxiv 2605.17625)
summary: Memory architecture combining episodic (session-level interaction records) and semantic (fact-level) stores for agents operating over long horizons; demonstrates improved task coherence across many steps.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — relevant to HID-188 (cross-run episodic memory); could strengthen the technical design of that issue but does not create a new gap. Not a new issue.

source: Red Queen Gödel Machine: Co-Evolving Agents and Evaluators (arxiv 2606.26294)
summary: Extension of Darwin Gödel Machine where both agents and their evaluators co-evolve in a Red Queen dynamic, producing more robust self-improvement without benchmark saturation.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — same category as Darwin Gödel Machine; requires evolutionary infrastructure and self-modification loops that are red-flagged in AgentForge's evaluation criteria.
